subject: The wave itself, cut through the plate along the line from strike to pickup and drawn as a beam between two fixed supports, with a force arrow, a probe to the output terminal and a dimensioned span.
controls: size: position, the supports move apart from a 120 px to a 380 px span and the dimension line follows, letting more half-waves fit.
tension: shape, the trace goes from a few broad bows to a stiffer, crinkled outline as upper modes stretch away.
damp: scale, the trace and its dashed envelope shrink from 44 px of swing to about 15 px.
pickup: position, the probe and its lead to the 'out' terminal slide along the span from the strike arrow toward the far support.
reference: library/theseus-tower (clean primitives, one line weight system) beside a stock waveform engine screen
risks: P3's own pitfall: it can drift into 'just an oscilloscope', and a 1D cut throws away the plate's second dimension, which is the whole idea of the machine. At rest the snapshot can sit nearly flat (the default looks calm, maybe too calm); damp as amplitude reads as 'level'. Schematic furniture (title block, chain line) is quiet but adds parts that no control owns.
